root.name: Ruy Lopez: Brix Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O g6

overview: Black meets the Morphy with a fianchetto instead of the main ...Be7 or ...b5, planning ...Bg7 and ...d6. White usually plays 6.d4 exd4 7.Nxd4 Bg7 or 6.Re1 and 7.c3, reaching an open Sicilian-like or slow Ruy centre, with the bishop pair of the Ruy pressing on c6. The line is solid for Black but gives White easy development and a slight space edge, which is why it is a rarely seen sideline.

white_ideas.idea: d4 and Nxd4 to open the centre and attack with Bxc6 and Nxc6 ideas
Re1, c3 and d4 with a typical Ruy centre

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the bishop and play ...d6, ...O-O and ...Re8
Trade the knights and bishop to ease the cramped position

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian-like structure after d4 exd4, or Ruy centre with a Black kingside fianchetto

character.notes: Black takes a safe, modern set-up where it is hard for White to land a quick blow.

soundness.notes: Playable; White keeps a slight edge but nothing decisive.

structure.notes: After d4 exd4 Nxd4 the e-pawn has been exchanged for the d-pawn and the d-file is half-open for White.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose it, preferring the main Ruy lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: Closed Ruy
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Be7
sublines_that_differ.how: The main line; this root is a different Black set-up.

character.reason: Black fianchettoes into a compact set-up that is hard to break down but passive.

soundness.reason: Fully playable, with White holding only a small edge.

structure.reason: The centre is unresolved; White chooses between d4 and a slower build-up.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose 5...g6 against the Ruy.

level.reason: Plans are clear and there is little forced theory.

plans.reason: Black plays ...g6 and ...Bg7 as the central idea.
